pre_change_state.caveat_quote: I read abstracts rather than full texts, and I ran about ten searches, so this is a map and not an exhaustive review.

claims.text: Pull the primary studies behind the meta-analysis [W2808281222] using `get_references`.
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: Instruction about a tool action, no checkable assertion about the paper.

claims.text: Telepresence robots for connectedness in dementia [W2751864896].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The integrative review is about telepresence robots for social connectedness in dementia.

claims.text: | [W2294211165] | PARO vs. dog vs. toy cat (randomized) | 100 nursing home residents, 12 visits each | Participants varied in cognitive impairment, so this is not strictly dementia-only. The dog and PARO drew the most physical contact, eye contact and speech. The more impaired the resident, the more interaction was directed to the animal. PARO did not hold attention over time. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches the abstract: randomized, 100 residents, 12 visits, dog and PARO drew most interaction, PARO attention declined, more impaired meant more interaction with the animal.

claims.text: PARO vs. real dog.** A study in a Spanish nursing home and day care centre (101 and 110 residents in two phases, plus 20 and 17 day-care patients) ran sessions twice a week for 3 months [W1807810766].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: Abstract does not say the nursing home was Spanish (location not given), and the dog arm was only in Phase 2 alongside PARO and control.

claims.text: I kept [W2294211165] (nursing home residents with varying cognitive impairment) and [W2080233792] (MCI and mild-to-moderate dementia) with a flag, but dropped [W2039822570] and [W1510372641], where dementia was simply unstated.
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W2294211165 and W2080233792 are described correctly, but the claim that W2039822570 and W1510372641 had dementia unstated is a process claim; W2039822570's abstract doesn't state dementia though, and the dropping is not in the records; overall not checkable as attributed.

claims.text: A social robot collecting patient-reported outcome measures from older patients [W2946005838].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The study had a social robot collect PROMs from older patients.

claims.text: **Robot companion cats at home** for people with dementia were studied in a qualitative case study [W3034490183].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Qualitative case study of robot cats for people with dementia at home.

claims.text: | [W2946005838] | Robot collecting patient-reported outcome measures | Older hospital patients |
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The study involved community-dwelling persons aged 70+, not hospital patients.

claims.text: A memory game with a socially assistive robot in a long-term care facility [W2003566851].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Brian 2.1 memory game case study in a long-term care facility.

claims.text: A related report on 10 residents with varying dementia, covering interaction modalities [W2040979576].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: 10 residents with varying dementia levels and interaction modalities.

claims.text: No significant change in quality of life, depression or perceived social support [W2955051104].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: MARIO abstract reports no significant differences in those outcomes.

claims.text: An earlier HRI paper reports first results from 18 households [W3137166629].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract reports first results from 18 private households.

claims.text: **Ethics.** Deception, attachment, and removing the robot at the end of a study come up in [W2778691880, W3001702224].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: W2778691880 covers ethics of giving/retrieving PARO; W3001702224 covers deception and attachment and distress if robot taken away.

claims.text: **The home companion robot field test** [W2717439789] focused on cognitive assistance for daily routines, with navigation and a shopping list.
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Cognitive assistance for daily routine, navigation and shopping list function are in the abstract.

claims.text: A humanoid robot for remote monitoring of nursing home residents [W2322289952].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Humanoid robot for remote monitoring of nursing home residents.

claims.text: **Exercise coaching robots** [W2065178260, W1967507142] are socially assistive robots that motivate exercise.
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both papers describe socially assistive robot exercise coaches motivating exercise.

claims.text: Also, three records I could not check at all: [W1178530349], [W2900350517] and [W2982896790].
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: Statement about the assistant's own process with a list of ids.

claims.text: **Single-session PARO study** [W2080233792]. 11 community-dwelling people with mild cognitive impairment or mild-to-moderate dementia (this is a mixed group).
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: 11 participants completed a single session; MCI or mild-to-moderate dementia.

claims.text: Depression and loneliness fell and quality of life rose [W3015603533].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Significant decreases in depression and loneliness and improved QoL during intervention.

claims.text: Eight-week group sensory therapy in a nursing home, with participants at varying cognitive impairment levels [W4243437205].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Eight-week sensory therapy at a nursing home with varying cognitive impairment.

claims.text: | [W4407738599] | PARO vs. stuffed animal in occupational therapy | Patients with dementia | The authors conclude robot therapy differs from therapy with inanimate objects and can encourage patients to be more self-directive. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches the abstract's comparison and conclusion.

claims.text: "Sunshine" chat robot [W3041860695] was a letter in which the abstract says only "cognitive impairment".
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract is a letter mentioning older adults with cognitive impairment only.

claims.text: An infection-control study of companion robots in care homes [W3081435517] is a practical read, not a dementia-specific one.
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Microbial contamination study of companion robots in care homes, not dementia-specific.

claims.text: | [W2894885829] | PARO vs. control (quasi-experimental) | 33 nursing home residents with dementia in Korea, 12 sessions | Significant differences in positive emotions and problem behaviours between groups. The PARO group improved significantly on social interaction. |
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: Abstract doesn't state Korea; also nonequivalent control, not 'PARO vs control' wrongly; the Korea location isn't in the record.

claims.text: **Facilitation matters.** Several studies describe staff or facilitator mediation as important [W3092218325, W2039822570 is related but not dementia-specific].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Facilitation needed in W3092218325; W2039822570 reports staff/family mediation and is not dementia-specific.

claims.text: **Control comparisons are mixed.** Plush toys often produced similar trends [W2074069593, W1505024467].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W1505024467 found stronger responses to PARO than the toy lion, so it does not show similar trends; only W2074069593 does.

claims.text: Robot-assisted therapy in institutionalized older adults [W1510372641]
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Title matches.

claims.text: Quality of life, depression and perceived social support did not change significantly [W2955051104].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: No significant differences in those measures.

claims.text: The home companion robot field test with eight seniors [W2717439789].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Eight senior volunteers in the field test.

claims.text: **Individual variation.** Reflections on a cluster RCT (PARO vs. plush toy vs. usual care) found considerable variation in how residents responded, and raised ethical questions about giving and retrieving the robot [W2778691880].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches cluster RCT reflections: variation in responses and ethics of giving and retrieving PARO.

claims.text: Attachment stayed low to medium, and perceived ease of use rose over time [W3001702224].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Attachment low to medium; perceived ease of use increased significantly.

claims.text: | [W1510372641] | Group PARO therapy in a pilot | "Institutionalized older adults" |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Group therapy with seal-like robot (Paro) in institutionalized older adults.

claims.text: Technical unreliability turned the robot into extra workload for therapists [W4251569456].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Technical problems turn robot into source of additional workload for therapists.

claims.text: A pilot RCT on chronic pain was reported as a conference abstract [W3097289914].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The record shows a pilot RCT but does not state it was a conference abstract.

claims.text: Matilda was trialed with 115 participants in residential care, with significant improvements in emotional, visual and behavioural engagement [W2564685734].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: 115 participants, significant engagement improvements.

claims.text: | [W2943699887] | Robot in an assisted-living community | Residents in general |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Social robot in assisted-living community.

claims.text: **AIBO, early dementia** [W2159536297]. 24 older people with small cognitive deficits (MMSE>23).
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: AIBO, 24 older subjects with MMSE>23.

claims.text: **Hobbit** [W2994761079, W3137166629] is described as an "assistive, social service robot".
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: W2994761079 describes Hobbit as assistive, social service robot; W3137166629 is a mobile social service robot prototype.

claims.text: A wearable soft-robotic glove for hand function in older adults, in a pilot RCT [W2966294143].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Pilot RCT of wearable soft-robotic glove for hand function in older adults.

claims.text: **Responses differ between people.** Cognitive impairment level moderated the response in several studies [W2732925385, W1505024467], and individual variation is stressed in [W2778691880].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W1505024467 does not report cognition level moderating response in the same way; W2732925385 and W2778691880 fit, but W1505024467 compares mild/moderate vs severe dementia, partially fits; still the 'cognitive impairment moderated' claim is only clearly in W2732925385.
